Guides

Website for associations: simple, useful and affordable

An association lives through the people who join it. But they still need to know it exists, what it does, and how to get involved. That is exactly what your website is for.

What an association’s website is for

Sports club, festival committee, parents’, neighbourhood or mutual aid association: the needs are similar. Your website must let someone who does not know you understand in one minute:

  • What you do, and for whom.
  • When and where your activities take place.
  • How to join or lend a hand.
  • Who to contact, without showing a volunteer’s personal number.

The problem of the volunteer who leaves

Many association websites were built by a dedicated member. The day they leave, nobody knows how to change the page any more, and the website stays stuck on the fête from three years ago.

With a plan, the website does not depend on any one person. Any committee member writes the request in the client area (“add the date of the general meeting”), and the change is made. When the committee changes, you just pass on the login.

An association budget

I know every expense goes to a vote. So the figures are easy to present at a meeting:

  • €250 once for a one-page website, with €62.50 when you order and €187.50 when it goes live.
  • €5 a month for the Chico plan: hosting, domain name, updates, two changes by Lia and one by Alex every month.

The rest of the creation price can also be spread over 6 or 12 months, at no extra cost.

Events and news

Two changes by Lia are enough to announce upcoming events. If your calendar is busy, the Power plan gives you 4, and the Lia + option adds ten more for €5 a month.

Memberships and donations

If you already use a service to collect memberships or donations, the website links to it with a clearly visible button. Otherwise, a downloadable membership form and a contact form do the job.

An address in your name

A domain name like your association’s name followed by “.fr” looks serious on a poster or a grant application. The guide to choosing a domain name helps you find it.

Your questions

Our association has very little money, is this reasonable?

The one-page website costs €250 just once, then €5 a month. Over a year, that is often less than printing the posters for one event.

Who can request changes?

Anyone the committee gives access to the client area. You can change the account’s password and email address when the team changes.

Can we put photos of our events on it?

Yes, that is actually what makes people want to join you. Just remember to get the consent of anyone recognisable, and of parents for children.
